Ramnenses.definition: Ramnēnsēs (Rhamn-) ium, m RAP, one of the three tribes of free citizens in the early Roman state (cf. Luceres, Taties): tres antiquae tribūs Ramnes, etc., L.: Quosque vocant Ramnes, O.— One of three centuries of knigh…

Rufulus.definition: Rufulus ī, m Rufus, a tribune of the soldiers elected by the army (from Rutilius Rufus, the author of the law permitting the election), L.

rabide.definition: rabidē adv. rabidus, madly, furiously : omnia appetens.

rabiose.definition: rabiōsē adv. rabiosus, ravingly, madly, fiercely : nihil iracunde rabioseve fecerunt.

radians.definition: radiāns antis, adj. P. of radio, beaming, shining : lumina solis, O.: Aquarius: luna, V.: aurum, O.: galea claro ab auro, O.—As subst m., the sun , C. poët.

radiatus.definition: radiātus adj. P. of radio, furnished with rays, irradiated, shining : sol: orbis flammeus solis, Att. ap. C.: lumina, O.

radior.definition: radior —, —, ārī radius, to gleam, beam, shine : galeae gemmis radientur, O.: radiabant lumine valvae, O.: radiant ut sidus ocelli, O.: in armis, Pr.

ramalia.definition: rāmālia ium, n ramus, twigs, shoots, sticks, brushwood : arida, O., Ta.

rapide.definition: rapidē adv. with comp. rapidus, hurriedly, rapidly : dilapsus (fluvius).—Fig.: quod (pathhtiko/n) cum rapide fertur: eo rapidius venire, Ta.

rapta.definition: rapta ae, f P. of rapio, a ravished one, seduced woman : gratus raptae raptor fuit, O.

raptum.definition: raptum ī, n P. of rapio, plunder, prey, booty : in diem rapto vivit, on daily plunder , L.: vivere ex rapto, O.: rapto potiri, V.

raptus2.definition: raptus (ūs), m RAP-, a snatching away, wrench : Inoo lacerata est altera (manus) raptu, by the violence of Ino , O.— A plundering, robbery : nullis raptibus aut latrociniis populantur, Ta.: penatium, of the house , Ta…

raro.definition: rārō adv. with comp. rarus, seldom, rarely, now and then : id, quod raro fit: evenire: vinum aegrotis prodest raro: Raro antecedentem scelestum Deseruit poena, H.: si rarius fiet, quam, etc.

ratus.definition: ratus adj. P. of reor, reckoned, fixed by calculation ; in the phrase, pro ratā parte, or pro ratā (sc. parte), in proportion, proportionally : militibus agros pollicetur, quaterna in singulos iugera, et pro ratā part…

rebellium.definition: rebellium ī, n rebellis, a revolt , L. dub.

recens1.definition: recēns entis (abl sing. entī; poet. also ente; gen plur. tium; poet. rarely tum, H.), adj. with comp. and sup, lately arisen, not long in existence, fresh, young, recent: iniuriae memoria, Cs.: amicus, new-made: omnis…

recens2.definition: recēns adv. 1 recens, lately, freshly, newly, just, recently : recens accepta cladis, L.: Sole recens orto, V.

receptum.definition: receptum ī, n P. n. of recipio, an engagement, obligation, guaranty : satis (est factum) nostro recepto: receptum intervertit.

receptus2.definition: receptus ūs, m re-+CAP-, a taking back, retraction, recantation : nimis pertinacis sententiae, L.—Of troops, a falling back, retiring, retreat, way of retreat : expeditum ad suos receptum habere, Cs.: ut nec receptum …

recessus2.definition: recessus ūs, m re-+CAD-, a going back, receding, retiring, retreat, departure : a pestiferis (rebus): ut luna accessu et recessu suo solis lumen accipiat: recessum primis ultimi non dabant, i. e. means of retreat , Cs…

recido1.definition: recidō or reccidō reccidī or recidī, recā sūrus, ere re-+cado, to fall back, spring back, return : in terras: ramulum adductum in oculum suum recidisse, had recoiled : (saxa) convulsa in eos recidebant, kept falling b…

recido2.definition: recīdō dī, sus, ere re-+caedo, to cut away, cut down, cut off : sceptrum imo de stirpe, V.: ceras inanī s, empty cells , V.: pueris membra, O.: volnus Ense recidendum est, O.: columnas, hew out , H.—Fig., to lop off, …

reclinis.definition: reclīnis e, adj. re+CLI-, leaning back, reclining : In sinu iuvenis, O.

reconditus.definition: reconditus adj. with comp. P. of recondo<*> put away, out of the way, hidden, concealed, retired, sequestered : tabulae et signa: quid Aegyptus? ut recondita est!: senatūs consultum, inclusum in tabulis, tamquam in va…

reconligo.definition: re-conligō (-colligō) lēgī, lectus, ere, to gather again, collect: etiam si cuius animus in te esset offensior, a me reconligi oportere, to be reconciled: te, i. e. take courage, O.: primos annos, regain, O.

recta.definition: rēctā adv. abl f. of rectus; sc. viā , straightway, straightforward, right on, directly . Tu rus hinc ibis? . . . rectā, T.: ab subselliis in rostra rectā: perge in exsilium: Tendimus hinc rectā Beneventum, H.

recte.definition: rēctē adv. with comp. and sup. rectus, in a straight line, straightly, undeviatingly : ferri.— Fig., rightly, correctly, properly, duly, suitably, appropriately, well, accurately : recte tu quidem, et vere: Tractare, …

rectum.definition: rēctum ī, n P. n. of rego, good, uprightness, rectitude, virtue : illud rectum, quod koto/rthwma dicebas: Neque id putabit, pravum an rectum siet, T.: curvo dignoscere rectum, H.: mens sibi conscia recti, V.: fidem re…

rectus.definition: rēctus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of rego, in a straight line, straight, upright, direct, undeviating : rectā regione iter instituere, L.: India, rectā regione spatiosa, Cu.: hinc in pistrinum rectā proficisci viā, T…

recuperatio.definition: recuperātiō (recip-) ōnis, f recupero, a getting back, regaining, recovery : libertatis.

recuperator.definition: recuperātor (recip-) ōris, m recupero, a regainer, recoverer : urbis, Ta.—Esp., one of a bench of three or five justices, for the summary trial of civil causes : recuperatorem dare: tris recuperatores dare, L.

recuperatorius.definition: recuperātōrius (recip-) adj. recuperator, of the recuperatores, of the special court for summary civil trials : iudicium.

recupero.definition: recuperō (recip-) āvī, ātus, āre CVP-, to get back, obtain again, regain, recover : erepta: amissa, Cs.: rem suam: fortunas patrias: arma, L.: rem p.: Formianum a Dolabellā: haec faciunt reciperandorum suorum causā, C…

redhibeo.definition: redhibeō —, itus, ēre red-+habeo.—Of goods purchased and found faulty, to give back, cancel the sale of : quae (vitia) nisi dixeris, redhibeatur mancipium.

redimiculum.definition: redimīculum ī, ae, n redimio, a band, fillet, necklace, chaplet, frontlet : haec civibus mulieri in redimiculum praebeat: habent redimicula mitrae, V., O.

redimio.definition: redimiō (imperf. redimībat, V.), —, ī tus, īre, to bind round, wreathe round, encircle, gird, wind, deck, crown: alcui tempora vittā, V.: mitrā capillos, O.: sertis redimiri et rosā?: redimitus coronis: redimitus temp…

redomitus.definition: 're-domitus P., resubdued, again conquered: cives (al. perdomiti).'

reductus.definition: reductus adj. P. of reduco, withdrawn, retired, remote, distant, lonely : sinūs, V.: in reductā valle, H.—Fig., withdrawn, removed, remote : Virtus est medium vitiorum et utriumque reductum, from either extreme , H.—P…

redux.definition: redux ducis (abl. reduce; poet. also reducī, O.), adj. re-+DVC-, that brings back, guiding back : Iuppiter, O.: unde, nisi te reduce, nulli ad penatīs suos iter est, Cu.— Led back, brought back, come back, returned : …

refert.definition: rē-fert or rē fert tulit, —, ferre, only 3 d pers., impers. or with pron n. as subj, it is of advantage, profits, befits, matters, imports, concerns, is of importance, is of consequence (often with gen. of price): at …

refertus.definition: refertus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of refercio, stuffed, crammed, filled full, thronged, crowded, replete : urbem opulentam refertamque cepit: refertius erit aerarium. omnibus rebus urbes: cupae taedā , Cs.: loca pr…

refervens.definition: re-fervēns ntis, adj., boiling over, hot: refervens falsum crimen, furious.

reflatus.definition: (reflātus) abl. ū, m reflo, a contrary wind : navī s delatas Uticam reflatu hoc.

regalis.definition: rēgālis ē, adj. rex, of a king, kingly, royal, regal : civitatis genus, ruled by kings : nomen (i. e. regio), title : sceptrum, O.: nomisma, H.: virtus et sapientia: ut sapere, sic divinare regale ducebant: virgo, a k…

regie.definition: rēgiē adv. regius, royally, imperiously, despotically : regie statuit in aratores, imperiously : crudeliter et regie factum.

regifice.definition: rēgificē adv. regificus, royally, magnificently, sumptuously : instructa domus, Enn. ap. C.

regressus.definition: regressus ūs, m re-+GRAD-, a going back, return, regress : conservare progressūs et regressūs constantes: regressū s dare viro, O.: Funditus occidimus neque habet Fortuna regressum, V.— A retreat : in tuto, L.—Fig., a…

reiectaneus.definition: rēiectāneus adj. reiectus, to be rejected, to be spurned.—Plur. n . as subst., transl. of a)poprohgme/na.

reiectio.definition: rēiectiō ōnis, f re-+IA-, a throwing back, rejection, repudiation : civitatis: iudicum, a challenging : reiectione interpositā .

relatus2.definition: relātus ūs, m re-+STER-, a report, recital : virtutem, Ta.: carminum, declamation , Ta.

relego1.definition: re-lēgō āvī, ātus, āre, to send away, send out of the way, despatch, remove, seclude: filium ab hominibus: (filium) rus supplici causā: relegati longe ab ceteris, Cs.: procul Europā in ultima orientis relegati senes, …

relego2.definition: re-legō lēgī, lēctus, ere, to gather together, collect again: Ianua filo est inventa relecto, i. e. by winding up the thread again, O.—To travel over, traverse again, retrace: litora, V.: Hellespontiacas aquas, O.—Fig…

religiose.definition: religiōsē adv. with comp. and sup. religiosus, conscientiously, scrupulously, punctually, exactly, carefully : testimonium dicere: iudicare: promittere, N.— With reverence for the gods, reverentially, piously, religio…

reminiscor.definition: reminīscor —, ī, dep. re-+1 MAN-, to recall to mind, recollect, remember : de quaestoribus: reminisceretur veteris incommodi populi R., Cs.: veteris famae, N.: Satyri, O.: reminiscere quae tradantur mysteriis: eas (re…

remisse.definition: remissē adv. with comp. remissus, gently, mildly, laxly : secum agere: nihilo remissius instare.

remissus.definition: remissus adj. with comp. P. of remitto, slack, loose, relaxed, languid : corpora: Venus et remisso Filius arcu, H.— Gentle, mild : remissior ventus, Cs.: remissiora frigora, Cs.—Fig., loose, slack, negligent, remiss :…

remote.definition: (remōtē) adv. remotus, at a distance, afar off .— Only comp: stellae aliae, remotius eadem spatia conficiunt.

remotus.definition: remōtus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of removeo, removed, far off, distant, remote, retired : silvestribus ac remotis locis, Cs.: Gades, H.: gramen, H.: domūs pars (i. e. penetralia), O.: remotius antrum, O.: sedes rem…

remuneror.definition: re-mūneror ātus, ārī, dep., to repay, reward, recompense, remunerate: gratiam in remunerando cumulare: remunerandi voluntas: te simillimo munere: magno se praemio, Cs.: quibus autem officiis Anni beneficia remunerabor…

renes.definition: rēnes (ium or um), m the kidneys, reins: umores, qui e renibus profunduntur: renes morbo temptentur acuto, H.

reno1.definition: re-nō āvī, —, āre, to swim back: saxa, i. e. rise to the surface, H.

reno2.definition: rēnō (rhēnō) ōnis, m Celtic, a deer-skin, garment, fur-cloak : rhenonum tegimentis uti, Cs.

reor1.definition: re- or red-. An inseparable particle, again, back, anew, against.

reor2.definition: reor ratus, ērī, dep. RA-, to reckon, calculate, believe, think, suppose, imagine, judge, deem : quos plurīs, quam rebar, esse cognovi: contra ac ratus erat, S.: Ut rebare, V.: ut ipse rebatur viam inexpugnabilem feci…

repens2.definition: repēns entis, adj., sudden, hasty, unexpected, unlooked for: cura, C. poët.: adventus consulis, L.: defectio, L.: cum fama repens alio avertit bellum, L.: discordia, V.: consternatio, Cu.—New, fresh, recent: quid repe…

repente.definition: repente adv. 2 repens, suddenly, unexpectedly, on a sudden : quamvis repente: a tergo signa canere, S.: cunctisque repente Improvisus ait, V.: conlecta auctoritas, Cs.: modo egens, repente dives: abiectus conscientiā …

repentino.definition: repentīnō adv. repentinus, suddenly, unexpectedly : mori: eruptionem facere, Cs.

repercussus2.definition: (repercussus ūs), m repercutio, a reverberation, echo .—Only abl sing. : quo gravior vox repercussu intumescat, Ta.

repexus.definition: re-pexus adj., combed anew, just combed: coma, O.

repletus.definition: replētus adj. P. of repleo, filled, full : Amnes, V.: cornu pomis, O.: his rebus exercitus, abundantly provided , Cs.: repletae semitae puerorum, L.—Fig.: eādem vi morbi, infected , L.

repositus.definition: 'repositus P. of repono; see also repostus.'

repostus.definition: repostus adj. P. of repono, remote, distant : penitus gentes, V.

repugnans.definition: repūgnāns antis, adj. P. of repugno, inconsistent, contradictory : res inter se.—Plur n . as subst, contradictory things, contradictions : locus ex repugnantibus.

repulsa.definition: repulsa ae, f P. of repello, a rejection, denial, refusal, repulse : ab repulsis eo magis debitum honorem repetentes, because of rejections , L.: nullam patiere repulsam, O.: Sint tua vota secura repulsae, O.: Veneris…

repulsus2.definition: (repulsus, ūs) m re-+1 PAL-, a reverberation, echo.— Plur. : scopulorum, C. poët.

requietus.definition: requiētus adj. P. of requiesco, rested, refreshed : miles, L.: ager, i. e. after lying fallow , O.

res1.definition: rēs reī, f RA-, a thing, object, matter, affair, business, event, fact, circumstance, occurrence, deed, condition, case : divinarum humanarumque rerum cognitio: te ut ulla res frangat?: relictis rebus suis omnibus: re…

resacro.definition: re-sacrō —, —, āre, to release from a curse, N.

rescriptum.definition: rēscrīptum ī, n rescribo, an imperial rescript , Ta.

resequor.definition: (re-sequor) secūtus, ī, dep., to follow, answer, reply: his contra alqm, O.: Pallada dictis, O.

reses.definition: (reses) idis, adj. re-+SED-, that stays behind, remaining, left : in urbe plebes, L.— Inactive, inert, sluggish, slothful, lazy, idle : eum residem intra vallum tempus terere, L.: residesque movebit Tullus in arma vir…

resilio.definition: resiliō uī, —, īre, to leap back, spring back: In gelidos lacūs, O.: ad manipulos velites, L.— To spring back, rebound, recoil, retreat: ferit ora sarissā. Non secus haec resilit, quam, etc., O.: In spatium resilire m…

resipisco.definition: resipīscō īvī or uī (resipīsset, C.), —, ere, inch. resipio, to recover the senses, come to, revive, recover : Resipisco, T.: resipisce, quaeso: quom te intellego Resipisse, have come to your senses , T.: ut tunc salt…

resistens.definition: resistēns ntis, adj. P. of resisto, enduring, firm : ad calamitates perferendas, Cs.

respectus2.definition: respectus ūs, m re-+SPEC-, a looking back, looking about : fugientibus miserabilem respectum incendiorum fore, the view behind them : sine respectu pugnabant, L.— A refuge, retreat, resort, asylum : ex acie respectum …

responsum.definition: respōnsum ī, n P. n. of respondeo, an answer, reply, response : exspectabat suis postulatis responsa, Cs.: haec ex illius ad nostra responsa responsis intellegentur: sine responso legatos dimisit, L.: tantis de rebus …

restricte.definition: restrictē adv. restrictus, closely, sparingly : facere.— Fig., strictly, exactly, precisely : cetera praefinio: praecipere.

restrictus.definition: restrictus adj. with comp. P. of restringo, bound fast, close, niggardly, stingy : eosdem restrictos fuisse: ad largiendum ex alieno restrictior.

resulto.definition: resultō —, ātus, āre, freq. resilio, to spring back, rebound : tela galeā resultant, V.— To reverberate, resound, re-echo : ubi vocis resultat imago, V.: colles clamore resultant, ring , V.

retempto.definition: re-temptō (-tentō) —, —, āre, to try anew, attempt again, reattempt: verba intermissa, O.: referoque manūs iterumque retempto, O.: studium fatale, O.: Saepe refringere vestīs, O.

retento1.definition: retentō —, —, āre, freq. retineo, to hold back firmly, keep back, hold fast : agmen, L.: admissos equos, O.— To preserve, maintain : sensūs hominum, C. poët.

retexo.definition: re-texō xuī, xtus, ere, to unweave, unravel: telam: tela retexta dolo, O.: Luna, retexuit orbem, i e. diminished again, O.—Fig., to undo, cancel, annul, reverse: novi timores retexunt superiora: illa (dicta), take bac…

retinacula.definition: retinācula ōrum, n retineo, a holdfast, band, tether, halter, halser, rope, cable : valida, L.: parant lentae retinacula viti, V.: mulae, H., O.

retinens.definition: retinēns entis, adj. P. of retineo, holding fast, tenacious, observant : libertatis: sui iuris, O.: moris, Ta.

retractus.definition: retrāctus adj. with comp. P. of retraho, drawn back, withdrawn, remote, distant : in intimo sinu, L.: retractior a mari murus, L.

retrorsum.definition: retrōrsum (C., H.) or retrōrsus (V.), adv. retroversus, back, backward, behind : vestigia nulla retrorsum, H.: mutata te ferat aura, H.: relegens errata retrorsus Litora, V.—Fig., in return, in reversed order : oritur…

retrusus.definition: retrūsus adj. P. of re-trudo, concealed, hidden, deep : simulacra deorum: haec in philosophiā.

retusus.definition: retūsus or retūnsus adj. P. of retundo, blunted, blunt, dull : ferrum, V.: Tela, O.—Fig.: ingenia.

reverens.definition: reverēns entis, adj. with comp. P. of revereor, respectful, reverent : sermo erga patrem, Ta.: reverentius visum credere, quam, etc., Ta.

reverenter.definition: reverenter adv. reverens, respectfully.— Comp. : reverentius duci parere, Ta.

revereor.definition: re-vereor itus, ērī, dep., to stand in awe of, regard, respect, honor, fear, be afraid of, reverence, revere: adventum tuom, T.: dicam non reverens adsentandi suspicionem: coetum virorum (Tullia), L.: fortunam captiva…

revertor.definition: re-vertor or re-vortor versus or vorsus, perf. usu. revertī (from reverto), ī, to turn back, turn about, come back, return: ex itinere: se vidisse exeuntem illum domo et revertentem: a ponte, H.: silvā, O.: domum: in …

revivisco.definition: re-vīvīscō vīxī, —, ere, inch. re+vivo, to come to life again, be restored to life, live again, revive : si Clodius revixerit: avum suum revixisse putat.—Fig., to revive, recover, gather strength, renew vigor : ex ill…

rhapsodia.definition: rhapsōdia ae, f , r(aywdi/a, a rhapsody, book (of a poem): secunda (of the Iliad), N.

rhetoricoteros.definition: rhētoricōteros ī, adj. comp., r(htorikw/teros, more oratorical, Lucil. ap. C.

rho.definition: rhō indecl., r(w=, the Greek letter r.

rictum.definition: rictum ī, n P. n. of ringor, the opening of the mouth, mouth opened wide : eius.

ridicule.definition: rīdiculē adv. ridiculus, laughably, jokingly, jestingly, humorously : rogas, T.: ridicule ac facete: dictum, Ph.— Absurdly, ridiculously : insanus.

rigens.definition: rigēns entis, adj. P. of rigeo, stiff, inflexible, rigid, unbending : unguis, O.: lorica ex aere, V.

rigide.definition: rigidē adv. rigidus, rigorously, severely , O.

rimor.definition: rīmor ātus, ārī, dep. rima, to lay open, tear up, turn up : rastris terram, V.: prata Caystri, grub through , V.— To tear up, turn over, pry into, search, examine, explore, ransack : alqd repertum, V.: Pectora pulloru…

rixor.definition: rixor ātus, ārī, dep. rixa, to quarrel, brawl, wrangle, dispute : cum eo de amiculā.

robus.definition: rōbus adj. RVB, red, ruddy : iuvencus, Iu.

rogatum.definition: rogātum ī, n P. of rogo, a question, interrogatory : nobis ad rogatum respondere, i. e. to the point : copiose ad rogata respondere.

rogatus.definition: (rogātus ūs), m rogo, a request, suit, entreaty (only abl sing .): rogatu tuo.

ros1.definition: rōs rōris, m dew: nocturnum excipere rorem, Cs.: Rore mero ieiunia pavit, O.: pecori gratissimus, V.: vitreus, O.: gelidos rores.—A trickling liquid, drops, moisture: Arabus, i. e. perfume, O.: Spargens rore levi, i. …

rosa.definition: rosa ae, f cf. r(o/don, a rose : Neu desint epulis rosae, H.: plena rosarum Atria, O.: cum rosam viderat, i. e. the latest of the spring flowers.—Sing. collect., roses, wreaths of roses : sertis redimiri iubebis et ro…

rotatus.definition: rotātus adj. P. of roto, well-rounded, concise : sermo, Iu.

rotunde.definition: rotundē adv. rotundus, roundly, smoothly, elegantly : apte ac rotunde.

rubens.definition: rubēns entis, adj. P. of rubeo, red, ruddy, reddish : Murice, V.: ver, V.: Dexterā, H.

ruber.definition: ruber bra, brum, adj. RVB-, red, ruddy : sanguis, H.: coccus, H.: Priapus, painted red , O.: oceani rubrum aequor, i. e. reddened by the setting sun , V.: Oceanus, the Eastern Ocean , H.: leges maiorum, with red title…

rubeta1.definition: rubēta ae, f a toad, Iu., Pr.

rubeta2.definition: rubēta ōrum, n rubus, bramble-thickets , O.

ructor.definition: rūctor —, ārī, dep. collat. form of ructo, to belch forth, belch up : versūs, H.

rudis2.definition: rudis is, f a slender stick, staff for exercise in fighting, quarter-staff, foil: (milites) rudibus inter se concurrerunt, L.: rudibus relictis Spicula promit, O.: rudem tam cito (accepisti)? (the gladiator received t…

rudus1.definition: rūdus (raudus) eris cf. rudis, a bit of copper (used as money, uncoined): rudera iacere, L.

rudus2.definition: rūdus eris, n broken stone, rubbish, debris: Ruderi accipiendo, Ta.: acutum silicis, Ct.

rustice.definition: rūsticē adj. with comp. rusticus, in a rustic manner, like a rustic : loqui.— Boorishly, rudely, clownishly : urgere: Rusticius tonsus, H.

ruta1.definition: rūta ae, f , r(uth/, a bitter herb, rue, C., O. —Fig., bitterness, unpleasantness: alcuius.

ruta2.definition: rūta ōrum, n P. plur. n. of ruo, things dug up, mining products, minerals , only in the phrase, ruta et caesa or ruta caesa, the crude products of an estate, timber and minerals : fundum vendere rutis caesis receptis,…
